evals.name: daily-audit-standard-run
evals.prompt: Run the daily Databricks cost audit. Credentials are already set as DATABRICKS_HOST/DATABRICKS_HTTP_PATH/DATABRICKS_TOKEN env vars.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/audit.py (no flags) to execute all enabled checks and persist findings, then presents a result led by total estimated monthly saving and the count of findings new today, followed by the top ~10 findings by est_monthly_saving_usd, and calls out any checks that were skipped rather than silently dropping them.
assertions: Runs scripts/audit.py rather than re-deriving the checks by hand or querying system tables ad hoc
Does not pass --dry-run or --no-write when the user asked to actually run the audit
The presented summary leads with total estimated monthly saving and the new-today count before the detailed findings list
Lists top findings ordered by est_monthly_saving_usd (highest first)
Explicitly mentions any skipped checks and why (e.g. a system table not enabled), rather than omitting them silently
Does not fabricate a specific dollar figure that did not come from the script's output
States clearly that dollar figures are estimates/list-price-based, not a bill

evals.name: missing-credentials
evals.prompt: Can you check our Databricks spend for cost savings? I haven't set up any credentials or told you which workspace.
evals.expected_output: Asks the user for DATABRICKS_HOST, DATABRICKS_HTTP_PATH, and DATABRICKS_TOKEN (or confirms where to find them) before attempting to run anything, rather than guessing a host/warehouse or fabricating findings.
assertions: Explicitly asks for the required connection details (host, HTTP path, token) rather than guessing them
Does not invent example findings, dollar figures, or a fake summary while credentials are missing
Does not claim to have run the audit when it has not
Does not silently fall back to a different workspace or default host

evals.name: dry-run-preview
evals.prompt: Before I give you write access to our billing tables, show me what the daily cost audit would actually check -- don't write anything or touch the findings table yet.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/audit.py --dry-run (or explains the checks without executing writes), printing/describing the SQL each check would run without creating the findings table or inserting any rows.
assertions: Uses the --dry-run flag (or otherwise avoids persisting anything) given the user explicitly asked not to write anything yet
Does not call ensure_table / CREATE TABLE / INSERT against the findings table in this run
Describes what the 10 (or 11 with C11 enabled) checks look for, matching the check list in SKILL.md
Does not present fabricated dollar findings as if a real run had already happened

evals.name: system-tables-not-enabled
evals.prompt: Run the full cost audit, but heads up -- I don't think query history or table lineage system tables are enabled in this workspace yet.
evals.expected_output: Runs the audit anyway, and when checks needing system.query.history or system.access.table_lineage fail/skip, explains why (schema not enabled) using references/system-tables.md, and tells the user how to enable those schemas rather than treating the partial run as a complete audit with no caveats.
assertions: Still runs the checks that don't depend on the missing schemas, rather than refusing the whole audit
Explicitly reports that checks needing system.query.history and/or system.access.table_lineage were skipped, and why
References how to enable the missing system-table schemas (the WorkspaceClient.system_schemas.enable pattern or admin console) rather than leaving the user stuck
Does not present the partial result as a complete 10-check audit without noting what was skipped
Does not fabricate query-history or lineage-based findings to compensate for the missing data
